articles.title: Hungarian investigators found $19.5 million in cash buried in forests and hidden in buildings while probing allegations against a former minister; treasury staff needed eight hours and five machines to count it
articles.summary: Viktor Orban ruled Hungary as the Prime Minister for 16 years from 2010 to 2026 and was characterised by systemic corruption and crony capitalism.
articles.body: Viktor Orban ruled Hungary as the Prime Minister for 16 years from 2010 to 2026 and was characterised by systemic corruption and crony capitalism. Evidence of the same has been appearing even after his term ended, with a long-awaited celebration in April this year. On Friday, Hungary's anti-corruption agency announced that it had seized cash worth $19.5M buried in forests and hidden elsewhere while investigating an ex-minister from Orbán's cabinet, as per a report by The Guardian.Miklós Seszták, Hungary’s minister of national development between 2014 and 2018, is accused of taking bribes in a scheme involving the state transport company, purchasing secondhand buses at inflated prices. Seszták, two other Orbán-era ministers and the former premier’s brother have been taken into custody in different cases as graft inquiries have gathered pace in recent weeks.The National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH), an anti-graft body with sweeping powers established as part of present Prime Minister Peter Magyar’s accountability drive, said it searched the capital of Budapest and three Hungarian counties on Thursday and Friday as part of the criminal proceedings against Seszták. The office holds investigative and prosecutorial powers to pursue cases of misused public funds and suspected corruption that Orbán’s critics say was rampant during his 16 years in office.“During the search, investigators found large amounts of cash: buried in forests, hidden in agricultural and warehouse buildings as well as residential properties, and stored in high-value safes in secluded locations,” the statement said. “The total amount of cash found during the two-day search was 5,071,632,000 forints, €2,658,350 and US $1,257,100,” it added, bringing the combined value to $19.5M. NVVH added that its staff deposited the cash into the Hungarian State Treasury's account. “Upon receipt, 12 Treasury employees spent 8 hours counting the money using 5 counting machines,” the finance minister, András Kármán, said on Facebook.A video posted to Facebook by the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office showed images of investigators kneeling next to extensive piles of bundled cash, as well as of shovels breaking ground in what appeared to be a forest at night.Sesztak has denied wrongdoing. According to Reuters, his lawyer Gabor Papp told the local news website Telex that the cash did not belong to Sesztak, a member of parliament's Economic and Energy Affairs Committee. He added that the bribery case also involved other suspects.Magyar hailed the seizure as a potential turning point. “This officially marks the end of the Fidesz-KDNP mafia!” he said in reference to Orbán’s former governing coalition. The 45-year-old Tisza leader won a landslide election victory in April, ending Orbán's 16 years in power. He also promised to investigate alleged corruption and abuse of office during his rival's rule. The clampdown is part of an anti-graft drive the centre-right Magyar has dubbed "Operation Purgatory", considered "very important" by 70% of respondents in a survey by the Median pollster released on news website HVG this week.Orban, on the other hand, has not reacted to the latest development. Previously, he had denounced the probes targeting his inner circle, dubbing them "political persecution" aimed at imprisoning him. Fidesz Party reacted to the announcement in a Facebook post, saying that it hoped Sesztak was not connected to the cash. "Since the change of regime, every lawmaker in Hungary has sworn an oath to abide by and enforce the law. Fidesz-KDNP (Christian Democrats) cannot associate itself with anyone who fails to do so. We trust that the images published by the NVVH (asset recovery office) have nothing to do with Miklos Sesztak," Fidesz wrote.Bence Retvari, parliamentary group leader of the Christian Democrats, said Sesztak, ⁠the party's vice chair, should relinquish his parliamentary mandate as he seeks to clear his name "This is an individual criminal case, and the criminal proceedings must be kept strictly separate from our political community," Retvari said on Facebook.You use AI every day. articles.title: How a Swedish missile took down Russia's 500 kmph drone over Ukraine
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Ukraine has intercepted a Russian jet-powered Geran-5 attack drone in the Kyiv region using Sweden’s RBS-70 air defence system for the first
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Ukraine has intercepted a Russian jet-powered Geran-5 attack drone in the Kyiv region using Sweden’s RBS-70 air defence system for the first time, according to the Ukrainian military. The interception marks a reported success against a faster variant of Russia’s attack drones, which can travel at speeds of more than 500 kmph and have an estimated range of up to 950 km.Ukraine’s General Staff announced on November 13 that personnel from the 1027th Anti-Aircraft Missile and Artillery Regiment had destroyed the drone using the Swedish-made system. It did not disclose the exact location or time of the interception.The regiment’s RBS-70 crew had earlier described the engagement in an interview with Ukrainian outlet LB.ua, published on November 11. A commander identified by the callsign Vigo said the drone was travelling at more than 500 kmph and descended towards its target only a few minutes before impact, leaving air defence crews with limited time to respond.Why the Geran-5 is harder to interceptUnlike the propeller-driven Geran-2 drones commonly used in Russia’s Shahed-style attacks, the Geran-5 is powered by a turbojet engine and has a conventional aircraft configuration.Ukraine’s Defence Intelligence Directorate (HUR) has said the drone resembles Iran’s Karrar and incorporates components also found in other Russian Geran models.According to HUR’s technical assessment released in January 2026, the Geran-5 has a maximum take-off weight of around 850 kg, a cruising speed of 450-600 kmph and an estimated range of up to 950 km. These figures are based on Ukrainian intelligence assessments and have not been independently verified.The drone’s higher speed reduces the time available for air defence crews to detect, identify and engage it. This makes the interception of jet-powered attack drones more challenging than countering slower, propeller-driven UAVs.How Sweden’s RBS-70 missile system worksDeveloped by Swedish defence company Saab, the RBS-70 uses laser beam-riding guidance, unlike several shoulder-fired air defence missiles that rely on infrared seekers to track an aircraft's heat signature.The operator keeps the target within the system's sight, while the missile follows a laser guidance corridor directed towards it. Since the missile does not depend on an infrared seeker, conventional heat-decoy flares are ineffective against its guidance system.The system is also less vulnerable to certain forms of electronic jamming that can interfere with radar-guided weapons. However, its guidance mechanism requires the operator to maintain a clear line of sight and continuously track the target during an engagement.The RBS-70 family has an engagement range of several kilometres, depending on the missile variant. Saab's newer RBS-70 NG configuration has an advertised range of more than 9 km and can engage targets at altitudes of up to 5 km.Sweden continues military support for UkraineSweden has supplied Ukraine with RBS-70 systems as part of its military assistance. In February 2025, the Swedish government announced an air defence package worth 1.2 billion Swedish kronor, or around $113 million at the time. The package included procurement of the latest RBS-70 version and Tridon Mk2 anti-aircraft systems for Ukraine.The latest interception is not the first reported Ukrainian success against the jet-powered Geran-5. In September 2026, Ukraine’s 1020th Anti-Aircraft Missile and Artillery Regiment released footage showing a Ukrainian-made STING interceptor drone destroying one of the Russian drones.Ukraine has also been exploring relatively affordable options to counter faster aerial threats, including interceptor drones and automated machine-gun systems.The latest engagement demonstrates how conventional short-range missile systems can also contribute to Ukraine’s air defence network as Russia expands its use of jet-powered attack drones.

articles.title: A man searching a Massachusetts dumpster rescued 1,132 ancient Mexican artefacts; more than 40 Connecticut high school students then spent almost two years cataloguing them before their return to Mexico
articles.summary: A routine house clearance in western Massachusetts nearly sent more than 1,100 pieces of Mexico's pre-Hispanic history to a landfill.
articles.body: A routine house clearance in western Massachusetts nearly sent more than 1,100 pieces of Mexico's pre-Hispanic history to a landfill. Instead, a man's decision to investigate unusual objects in a dumpster set off an unlikely rescue operation involving an archaeologist and more than 40 high school students in Connecticut. According to a joint announcement by Mexico's Foreign Affairs and Culture ministries on August 17, 2026, all 1,132 objects were eventually returned to the Mexican Consulate in Boston after nearly two years of work to clean, classify, catalogue and document them.The discovery began around two-and-a-half years before the handover, when Matthew Pioggia was helping clear an old house in western Massachusetts. Among the discarded belongings in a dumpster, he noticed objects that appeared unusual. Knowing that his relative by marriage, Jeremy Pilver, was an archaeologist, Pioggia photographed some of the items and sent him the pictures, hoping he could identify them.Pilver, who teaches archaeology at Farmington High School in Connecticut, immediately recognised that the objects appeared to be genuine archaeological material. Although he could not initially determine their precise cultural origin or age, he realised they needed to be rescued before the dumpster was emptied. He urged Pioggia to retrieve as many as possible.In an interview with NPR, Pilver recalled that Pioggia climbed into the dumpster and spent about four hours digging through the discarded material. The objects were mixed with personal belongings, household debris and other waste. Pioggia eventually brought Pilver around 50 box tops filled with recovered material. The collection was in poor condition, with dust and debris covering the objects and their containers. Pilver also noticed evidence that mice and other animals had been around them.What followed was a painstaking project that turned a high school classroom into an archaeological workspace. Pilver enlisted his students to help examine and document the collection. Over nearly two years, more than 40 students participated in cleaning the surfaces of the objects, sorting and classifying them, creating a digital inventory and database, taking photographs, documenting individual pieces and preparing them for professional packing.Archaeological collections also carry information through their materials, designs, condition and associations. Recording those details systematically helps researchers study and compare objects, particularly when their original excavation context is not fully known. Pilver told NPR that the students worked through the collection using a shared spreadsheet and were deeply engaged in the project. He described the experience as an opportunity to show them the less glamorous but essential laboratory work behind archaeology.As the students worked through the boxes, they also uncovered an important clue to the collection's history. Pioggia had rescued paperwork along with the objects. According to Pilver, the documents indicated that the artefacts had been loaned from Mexico City's National Museum of Archaeology to a researcher connected with a US university around 55 years earlier. The paperwork provided a link to their Mexican origins, although it did not establish exactly how the collection eventually ended up in the Massachusetts house or why it was discarded.The inventory was subsequently assessed by specialists from Mexico's National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH). Their examination identified the collection as pre-Hispanic archaeological material originating in southeastern Mexico. It included objects from different periods, meaning their precise dates and cultural associations still need further investigation. The documentation supplied by Pilver is expected to help specialists establish more details about the collection's provenance and chronology.The largest category consisted of 1,053 ceramic fragments, many of them believed to have been used for domestic purposes. The pieces included smoothed, moulded, painted and incised pottery. The collection also contained two complete spindle whorls, objects traditionally used in textile production, and 18 fragments of figurines. Other recovered material included nine flakes of obsidian, a volcanic glass commonly used by ancient communities to make tools, and 11 flint flakes. The inventory also recorded three wood fragments, three stone polishers, an incomplete slab of metamorphic rock, a fragment of another stone slab and 36 shark teeth associated with the archaeological material.The objects were not all elaborate or immediately recognisable as historical treasures. Some were fragments of everyday pottery, while others included small decorative pieces. In his NPR interview, Pilver described a small bird-shaped pendant that may have been worn on a necklace and an object he believed could have been an ear ornament. Their significance lay not only in their appearance but also in what they could reveal about the people and communities that made and used them.For Pilver, identifying the objects was only one part of the responsibility. He believed they belonged to the people and culture from which they originated and that returning them was the ethical course of action. He coordinated with the Mexican Consulate General in Boston, the Foreign Affairs Ministry and INAH to arrange the voluntary handover. The students also helped photograph, document and professionally pack the collection for its journey back.In August 2026, the consulate formally received all 1,132 objects during a handover ceremony. Mexico's government described the collection as one of the largest archaeological groups received by the Boston consulate in recent years. The return was coordinated by the consulate in collaboration with INAH, the Foreign Affairs Ministry and academic institutions in the New England region.Speaking to NPR, Pilver described the handover as an enormous relief after more than two years of work. He recalled how consulate staff came out to receive the boxes one by one, saying he felt as though he had taken his first deep breath in about two-and-a-half years. He was particularly moved by the response of Mexican officials, who recognised the significance of the gesture.The project also gave the students an unusual opportunity to put archaeological ethics into practice. Instead of learning about cultural heritage and repatriation only through textbooks and classroom discussions, they were directly involved in documenting and returning objects to their country of origin. Their contribution extended beyond identifying and sorting the pieces to creating a record that can support future research.Mexico's Culture Ministry said the documentation provided by Pilver would be used to establish further dating and provenance information, potentially allowing the objects to serve as a comparative collection for academic study. The return also forms part of the country's wider efforts to recover archaeological and historical material held abroad.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A man took a painting left on a Seville street for its gold frame; an auction house said it may be a Sorolla worth an estimated €40,000–€150,000, and he returned it
articles.summary: A visitor in Seville found a painting valued at up to €150,000 mistakenly left on the street. Instead of keeping it, he returned it to its rightful owners after discovering it was an original Joaquín Sorolla.
articles.body: A man visiting Seville, Spain, picked up a painting left on the street because he liked its gold frame. He learned that it was believed to be an original work by Spanish artist Joaquín Sorolla, valued at up to €150,000. Instead of keeping it, he contacted police and helped return it to the owners. EuroNews reported that Andrés Hurtado was 57 and visiting Seville from Murcia. The Guardian described the painting as showing two boats off a beach. He did not initially realise that a small artwork could be so valuable. Hurtado found the painting on Saturday, June 27, 2026, while visiting Seville with his family, according to The Guardian.The family had accidentally left the painting behindIt was in the possession of a family residing in Seville, who had kept the artwork for many years. The family was getting ready for a vacation to the beach and decided to carry the painting along. While packing, one of the members left the painting outside their house. Their family left without realising that the painting was no longer in their possession. They came back to search for the painting, but failed to find it. As stated in Europa Press, they reported the loss to the police and put out notices in the locality for the recovery of the lost painting. The family described the painting as something very dear to them. In the request for the return of the painting, they neither revealed the artist’s name nor its market value. On the other hand, Hurtado took the painting to Murcia. He first concentrated on the frame of the painting before anything else. After closer examination, he found the signature and was interested in knowing more about the artist.AI and an auction house helped identify the paintingHurtado used an AI tool to analyse the painting and the result suggested it may have been painted by Joaquín Sorolla, one of Spain’s most celebrated painters. Hurtado then contacted an auction house in Madrid and sent them photos of the painting. Based on those pictures, they said it looked like a genuine Sorolla and estimated its value at between €40,000 and €150,000. This was a preliminary opinion and not an independent authentication.According to Encyclopedia Britannica, Joaquín Sorolla was born in 1863 and died in 1923. He was well known for his paintings of sunlight, water and daily life along the Spanish coast. His beach scenes used vibrant colours and played with reflections on the water.Hurtado contacted the police to return the artworkHurtado then saw the reports and photographs the family had circulated of the missing painting. He recognised the painting and called the police, explaining that he had only picked it up because he liked the frame. He added that he did not steal the painting, but wanted to give it back since he discovered its true identity and value. The police identified the artwork and helped return it to its owners, who thanked Hurtado. The Guardian reported that the family promised Hurtado a “small present” as thanks for returning the painting. For Hurtado, the discovery also revealed that an artwork he had picked up almost by chance could be worth far more than the frame that first caught his attention.You use AI every day. articles.title: Global droughts expose Texas dinosaur tracks, Yangtze statues, revealing climate change's surprising impact on archaeology
articles.summary: Explore how recent droughts in Texas and China have revealed significant archaeological finds, including ancient dinosaur tracks and historic Buddhist statues, while highlighting the impact of climate change on heritage preservation.
articles.body: Droughts can change landscapes in unexpected ways. As rivers shrink and reservoirs lose water, objects hidden beneath their surfaces can become visible. These discoveries give scientists opportunities to study the past, but they can also expose fragile remains to environmental damage. In August 2022, drought and heat revealed prehistoric dinosaur tracks in Texas and historic Buddhist statues from underneath the Yangtze River in China. These discoveries were noteworthy in terms of their significance in history. They also demonstrated how changes in the environment can have an effect on archaeological sites. While it is not possible to state that climate change is the reason for either discovery, it does increase the chances of extreme weather events.Texas drought reveals 113-million-year-old dinosaur footprintsThe dinosaur prints came into view in August 2022 as water levels dropped in the Paluxy River. According to the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department, the prints are about 113 million years old and normally sit underwater, often buried in sediment. According to the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department, the prints emerged when dinosaurs left their tracks on muddy tidal flats near the old sea, which eventually became hard and turned into limestone. Several prints belonged to Acrocanthosaurus, a big two-legged carnivorous dinosaur. Other prints came from Sauroposeidon, a huge long-necked, plant-eating dinosaur, according to the park. The prints gave insight into how dinosaurs lived and moved in ways that were not visible through skeletal fossils of dinosaurs. However, the discovery raised preservation concerns, since the prints are normally covered by water and sediment in the river. Once exposed, the limestone is more vulnerable to erosion.Yangtze River drought exposes historic Buddhist statuesAccording to Reuters, a similar discovery was made in Chongqing, southwestern China, in August 2022 during a severe drought. Falling water levels in the Yangtze River exposed Foyeliang, a reef that is normally submerged, along with three Buddhist statues, according to Xinhua, China’s state news agency. The statues are believed to be around 600 years old and were initially identified as dating from the Ming and Qing dynasties. There were reports of a monk statue that was seated on a lotus pedestal. This discovery gave insight into the region's past religion and culture. However, such sudden exposure created problems regarding the preservation of submerged cultural sites. Changing water levels leave these stone carvings exposed to sunlight, temperature swings and erosion.Research identifies climate risks to heritage sitesThe discoveries reflect a wider concern among heritage researchers. Climate change can intensify environmental conditions that threaten archaeological and palaeontological remains. A 2022 research article, “Climate Change and the Loss of Archaeological Sites and Landscapes: A Global Perspective,” discussed how climate change was creating new risks for archaeological sites and worsening existing vulnerabilities. The article identified increased rainfall, more extreme weather, rising sea levels and higher temperatures as pressures on archaeological landscapes. It also looked at how these changes affect different heritage sites and what archaeologists and conservation experts do to protect them. A separate 2025 study, “World Cultural Heritage sites are under climate stress and no emissions mitigation pathways can uniformly protect them,” published in Communications Earth & Environment, examined 938 UNESCO cultural heritage sites.The researchers found that about 80% of the studied sites were already experiencing climate stress and nearly 19% faced stress above the damage thresholds for both stone and wood. From the above-mentioned research, it can be understood that various types of building materials react differently to stress.Why does sudden exposure threaten historical discoveries?Drought has allowed researchers to uncover artefacts that are normally underwater and out of reach. However, long exposure to such environmental conditions could contribute to degradation. The examples of the discoveries in Texas and the Yangtze River clearly indicate this issue. While decreasing water levels have led to the uncovering of historical artefacts, the same factors have made them susceptible to environmental conditions. Such cases do not prove climate change as the cause of these discoveries.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 1967, an X-15 test flight killed Major Michael Adams; a remote California monument now marks the crash site of the experimental aircraft
articles.summary: Explore the final flight of X-15 and the tragic accident that took Major Michael Adams' life, shaping aerospace research and safety protocols at the edge of space.
articles.body: The North American X-15 helped researchers explore hypersonic flight and the conditions aircraft face near the edge of space. Its experimental flights advanced aerospace research, but one mission in 1967 ended in disaster. According to NASA.gov, U.S. Air Force Major Michael J. Adams lost his life when his aircraft broke apart during descent, leaving investigators to examine how technical problems, pilot workload and limited ground monitoring contributed to the accident.Michael Adams reached the edge of space before the fatal crash On November 15, 1967, Major Michael J. Adams took X-15 No. 3 on his seventh flight in the program. X-15 No. 3 was launched by an NB-52B carrier aircraft at an altitude of about 45,000 feet over Delamar Dry Lake, Nevada. In the flight, he achieved an altitude of 266,000 feet or 50.38 miles. This entitled him to receive the U.S. Air Force astronaut wings according to the altitude requirements. But soon enough, there were problems with the mission. As stated by NASA.gov, electrical disturbances early in the flight distracted Adams and made the aircraft control system less effective.During the wing rocking maneuver, the motions of the aircraft became too much and caused it to drift from its course. The X-15 then went into a spin at Mach 5 at around 230,000 feet. Adams recovered from the spin at 118,000 feet. But the aircraft then went into an inverted dive at Mach 4.7. There was a sustained oscillation with the MH-96 adaptive flight control system, which made the aircraft more difficult to control. The X-15 was flying at Mach 3.93 at around 65,000 feet. The aircraft experienced vertical loads exceeding 15 g and lateral loads of 8 g before breaking apart northeast of Johannesburg, California, 10 minutes and 35 seconds after launch.NASA’s investigation identified interacting causesThe accident investigation examined several factors rather than attributing the crash to one isolated failure. NASA’s 2014 assessment, A Comprehensive Analysis of the X-15 Flight 3-65 Accident, revisited the accident and examined the relationship between aircraft malfunctions, pilot workload and the adaptive flight control system.Adams had to interpret cockpit data in connection with the electrical upset and a challenging hypersonic flight condition. The investigators also took into account the possibility that the pilot experienced spatial disorientation during the interpretation of the aircraft movement. The ground controller had their own set of difficulties. They did not have current heading information and could not interpret the movement of the aircraft properly. The original accident board had made certain recommendations, which included a telemetered heading device for ground controllers and the screening of X-15 pilots for vertigo.California memorial marks the crash siteAdams’s astronaut wings were awarded posthumously because his flight went beyond 50 miles. His name was added to the Astronaut Memorial at the Kennedy Space Center in 1991. A second memorial to Adams was dedicated in 2004 near the crash site in California. The memorial sits in the Mojave Desert, northeast of Johannesburg, near where the experimental aircraft crashed. Its remote location follows from where the accident happened.The X-15 programme continued until 1968Even after the loss of Adams and his aircraft, research with the X-15 continued. The November 15 flight was the last for X-15 No. 3 and the 191st flight of the program overall. In all, the X-15 fleet flew 199 times before the program ended on October 24, 1968. According to NASA’s historical records, the X-15 contributed to research on hypersonic flight and aircraft performance. Finally, the tragic accident of Adams was a clear demonstration of the significance of the flight control system, reliability, the precision of instrument measurements and efficient communication between pilots and crews on the ground.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Bomb planted at CSMT': Security agencies, dog squad launch hours-long search after caller warns of blast at Mumbai station
articles.summary: MUMBAI: A major security operation was launched at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) on Saturday evening after authorities received a phone call
articles.body: MUMBAI: A major security operation was launched at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) on Saturday evening after authorities received a phone call warning of a bomb blast at the busy railway station. The threat, however, turned out to be a hoax after an extensive search of the premises.According to officials, the Government Railway Police (GRP) Control Room at Wadi Bunder received information around 6.40pm about a caller claiming that an explosive device had been planted at CSMT.Following the alert, multiple security agencies swung into action and initiated a comprehensive combing operation across the station.Teams from the Railway Protection Force (RPF), Government Railway Police, Mumbai Police and other security units carried out a coordinated search of the station complex.An RPF dog squad was also deployed to scan key areas, including suburban and long-distance train platforms, foot overbridges and the parcel office.Security personnel thoroughly checked parked trains and various sections of the station to ensure passenger safety.The operation continued for several hours amid heightened vigilance, though railway services were not disrupted.Central Railway chief spokesperson Swapnil Nila said that no suspicious object, explosive material or suspect individual was found during the search.Following the exhaustive sweep, officials declared the bomb threat a hoax.Authorities are now working to trace the caller and determine the source of the threatening message.They reiterated that strict action would be taken against those responsible for creating panic and misusing emergency response systems.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: NFL star Fred Warner and wife Sydney support pregnant women and single mothers through a San Jose charity, hosting a dinner and donating essential supplies to families in crisis
articles.summary: During the NFL season, much of Fred Warner’s time is taken up by training, matches and commitments with the San Francisco 49ers.
articles.body: During the NFL season, much of Fred Warner’s time is taken up by training, matches and commitments with the San Francisco 49ers. But away from the field, the linebacker and his wife, Sydney, have also been making time for a cause rooted in their own family experiences. The couple recently brought together single mothers and their children for an evening in the Bay Area, combining a shared meal with donations of everyday essentials. The gathering was organised in partnership with a San Jose organisation that provides residential support to pregnant women and new mothers dealing with difficult circumstances.Fred and Sydney Warner host dinner for single mothers and donate essentialsAccording to the San Francisco 49ers, the gathering, hosted by Fred and Sydney Warner, was held in collaboration with CityTeam’s Heritage Home programme. Mothers and children sat down for a meal in an outdoor setting, while supplies donated for the families were made available nearby.The contributions included blankets, nappies, toys and other household essentials. The evening also gave the couple an opportunity to spend time with the women receiving support, rather than simply make a donation through an organisation.The Instagram post shared on social media showed the Warners, accompanied by their young daughter Bella, interacting with guests. The couple were seen greeting and embracing some of the mothers before joining them for dinner.Both raised by single mothers, Fred and Sydney Warner share a message of supportFor Fred and Sydney, supporting single mothers was connected to their own upbringing. Both were raised by single mothers, an experience Sydney discussed in an Instagram post documenting the event.She spoke about how their mothers managed the difficulties of raising children while dealing with personal challenges of their own. Their experiences, she suggested, had influenced the way both she and Fred approached family life and their understanding of the pressures faced by women raising children without a partner.The couple also used the gathering to speak directly to the mothers. Sydney told the women that the circumstances they were currently facing did not have to determine what lay ahead for them or their children.Fred, meanwhile, thanked the guests for allowing the couple to be part of the evening. He said they were grateful to be in a position to offer assistance and wanted to support the families in whatever way they could.What CityTeam’s Heritage Home providesThe event was organised alongside CityTeam, a non-profit organisation working with people affected by homelessness, poverty, hunger and addiction. Its programmes include residential services for women who need support during pregnancy and after giving birth.Heritage Home, based in San Jose, offers free accommodation and assistance to pregnant women and new mothers experiencing crisis situations. The programme provides a residential setting for women who may be dealing with housing insecurity or other personal difficulties during a particularly demanding period of their lives.By bringing donations and a shared meal to families connected with the programme, the Warners' visit offered practical assistance alongside an opportunity for the women to spend time together.The event also reflected a form of community involvement that has a direct connection to the couple's own family histories. For the mothers who attended, the evening included both donated essentials for their children and an opportunity to meet people who wanted to support them.You use AI every day. articles.title: Missing for 2 months, Sambalpur driver found murdered; friend held
articles.summary: Sambalpur police recovered missing driver Rajesh Gupta’s skeletal remains after 2.5 months; friend Bhagaban Tandi held for alleged murder during drinking.
articles.body: Sambalpur: The mystery surrounding the disappearance of a 32-year-old driver nearly two-and-a-half months ago has turned into a murder case after police recovered his skeletal remains from under a bush and detained his friend for allegedly killing him following an argument during a drinking session.Police said the victim, Rajesh Gupta, was allegedly bludgeoned to death with a stone by 38-year-old Bhagaban Tandi of Bhuyanpada, who then hid the body under a bush. Tandi has been detained and is being questioned.Sambalpur Sadar SDPO Tofan Bag said Rajesh, a resident of Krishnanagar, had left home for work on Aug 26 and did not return. His brother lodged a missing person complaint at Bareipali police station on Sept 27.Rajesh, who worked as a driver and stayed with his elder brother in Sambalpur, frequently travelled outside for work and would sometimes return after 20 to 25 days. His family, therefore, initially did not suspect anything amiss.During the investigation, police received information that Tandi had allegedly admitted in front of another person that he had killed Rajesh while under the influence of alcohol. Following the tip-off, a special team comprising personnel from Bareipali and Ainthapali police stations was formed on the direction of Sambalpur SP.Police subsequently detained Tandi for questioning. Based on information provided by him, a police team, accompanied by a sniffer dog squad and scientific personnel, searched the suspected crime spot.The victim’s skeletal remains and bones were recovered from under a bush in the presence of a magistrate, police said. The remains were sent to the forensic medicine and toxicology department for postmortem examination.Rajesh’s elder brother, Rajan Gupta, said his brother earned his livelihood by driving and alleged that his behaviour had changed after he became friends with Tandi. articles.title: Australia, Philippines sign defence pact amid China tensions: Why Beijing is worried
articles.summary: Australia and the Philippines on Sunday signed a defence cooperation agreement aimed at streamlining joint military activities and strengthening security
articles.body: Australia and the Philippines on Sunday signed a defence cooperation agreement aimed at streamlining joint military activities and strengthening security ties, a move that could deepen regional coordination amid tensions with China in the South China Sea.The Defence Cooperation Arrangement (DCA) will simplify procedures under the bilateral Status of Visiting Forces Agreement (SOVFA), making it easier for the two countries to coordinate military activities involving their maritime, air and land forces.Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro said the agreement would reduce bureaucratic hurdles and strengthen Manila's ability to respond to security challenges."Rather than 100 steps to do a single thing, it will just now take 10," Teodoro told reporters, describing the deal as an "anti-red tape measure" for implementing SOVFA.He said the arrangement would also facilitate cooperation in humanitarian assistance and disaster response, while bolstering the Philippines' "credible deterrence posture", including in the South China Sea.Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese witnessed the signing in Manila, where he is attending a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). He said the agreement would improve maritime awareness and information sharing, while expanding strategic dialogue, military training, interoperability and defence infrastructure development.Albanese also announced additional Australian investment in maritime domain awareness, including drone technology, equipment and training to improve the detection of maritime and cybersecurity threats.China's defence and foreign ministries did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the agreement on Sunday.Why is China concerned about the pact?The agreement comes as the Philippines expands its security partnerships with countries including Australia, the United States and Japan amid repeated tensions with China over competing territorial and maritime claims in the South China Sea.Australia has consistently backed Manila's position on the strategic waterway and supported the 2016 ruling by an international arbitral tribunal, which rejected the legal basis of China's expansive claims in the South China Sea. Beijing has rejected the ruling and maintains that its actions in the disputed waters are lawful.The latest agreement could make military coordination between Australia and the Philippines easier, including through joint exercises, training and information sharing. The proposed expansion of maritime surveillance capabilities, particularly through Australian investment in drone technology, could also improve Manila's ability to monitor activity in the disputed waters.For Beijing, closer military coordination between Manila and its security partners could complicate its efforts to deal with the Philippines bilaterally over maritime disputes.China has repeatedly opposed joint military activities involving the Philippines and countries outside the region, arguing that such exercises increase tensions in the South China Sea.Philippines seeks wider security partnershipsThe agreement reflects Manila's efforts to broaden its network of defence partnerships beyond its longstanding treaty alliance with Washington.Australia, the US, Japan and the Philippines have stepped up military cooperation in recent years, including through joint maritime activities and exercises in the Indo-Pacific.In February, the four countries conducted joint patrols in the waters and airspace around China's Huangyan Dao, also known as Scarborough Shoal. The activities drew criticism from Beijing.China's defence ministry spokesperson Zhang Xiaogang had accused countries outside the region of increasing tensions through their military presence in the South China Sea."countries outside the region, such as the US, have traveled thousands of kilometers to the South China Sea to flex their muscles and stir up tensions. They are the real source of uncertainty," Zhang said.He also accused the Philippines of seeking external support to pursue its claims and warned that the Chinese military would respond to what it considers provocative actions."The Chinese military remains on high alert and will take resolute countermeasures against any rights-violation and provocative acts," Zhang said.Can the 'Squad' emerge as a regional security bloc?The growing defence cooperation among Australia, the US, Japan and the Philippines has also fuelled discussion about an informal security grouping known as the 'Squad'.The four countries have increased joint military activities and cooperation, with a focus on strengthening the Philippines' defence capabilities amid tensions with China.However, questions remain over whether the grouping can evolve into a more formal security arrangement similar to the Quad, which brings together India, the US, Japan and Australia.Chinese military affairs expert Song Zhongping told the Global Times that Manila was seeking to involve more external powers in the South China Sea dispute because it could not contend with China on its own.He said Australia's involvement would largely depend on Washington's approach to the region, adding that Canberra was unlikely to adopt a more aggressive position if the US chose to limit its involvement.Song also questioned whether the four countries could maintain a unified approach, saying the grouping's cohesion would depend largely on Washington's willingness to drive the initiative.The latest agreement strengthens military coordination between Australia and the Philippines. However, whether this translates into a more coordinated regional security framework will depend on the strategic priorities of all four countries.

articles.title: An Iranian shipping businessman left his $3.2 million in US assets to the eldest of his three daughters, a jury sided with her, and now a Maryland appeals court has ordered a new hearing for her two sisters
articles.summary: An inheritance dispute over nearly $3.2 million in US assets left by an Iranian shipping businessman has returned to court after a Maryland appeals court
articles.body: An inheritance dispute over nearly $3.2 million in US assets left by an Iranian shipping businessman has returned to court after a Maryland appeals court overturned a jury's decision in favour of his eldest daughter. The case centres on whether Seyedkazem Amini-Nejad, who died in 2023 at the age of 95, understood the estate documents that left his American assets exclusively to one of his three daughters. In a ruling dated October 28, 2026, the Appellate Court of Maryland said the jury had been given an incorrect legal standard when considering the younger daughters' claim that their sister deliberately interfered with their expected inheritance.Amini-Nejad had spent most of his life in Iran, where he co-owned a shipping company with two business partners. He travelled to the United States to visit his family and receive medical treatment. All three of his daughters lived in the US, and the eldest, Ellahe Amini-Nejad, had been involved in managing his finances and accompanying him to medical and legal appointments during his visits.The dispute arose from estate-planning documents signed during a visit to the US in March 2019. On March 22 that year, Amini-Nejad signed a will stating that his cash, liquid assets, stocks, shares, bank accounts, life insurance policies and retirement benefits should go to Ellahe. She was also named the executor and personal representative of the will. A trust was established soon afterwards, with Ellahe named as its sole trustee and beneficiary. Court records show that $3,199,794 was transferred into the trust. The documents did not name his younger daughters, Elham and Eman, as beneficiaries.The arrangements became contentious after Amini-Nejad died on May 23, 2023. The younger sisters said they had not been informed about the will or trust and discovered the documents only after travelling to Iran for their father's funeral. While searching through his belongings at the family home in Tehran, they found a folder containing estate papers, bank documents and handwritten notes in Farsi.The notes became an important part of their challenge. Elham testified that she was certain the handwriting on a note attached to the will belonged to her eldest sister. The younger daughters argued that their father spoke limited English and could not have adequately understood the English-language legal documents he had signed. They also maintained that he had wanted his three daughters to remain united and share his estate.The sisters filed a lawsuit in Maryland in January 2024, alleging fraud, undue influence, intentional interference with their expected inheritance and financial exploitation. They sought to have the trust invalidated and compensation for the assets they believed had been wrongfully diverted.During the trial, the eldest daughter disputed the allegations and maintained that her father had independently chosen how to distribute his American assets. The attorney who prepared the estate documents testified that he communicated with Amini-Nejad in both Farsi and English and believed his client understood the arrangements and was acting voluntarily. The court also heard that all three daughters had accompanied their father to appointments during his visits to the US.The younger sisters pointed to another decision their father had made: in August 2021, he transferred the deed of the family home in Tehran to all three daughters. They argued that this was consistent with his wish to treat them equally. They also questioned why the will and trust had not been disclosed to them while their father was alive.After a four-day trial in Howard County Circuit Court, the jury found that Elham and Eman had a reasonable expectation of receiving an inheritance. However, it ruled in favour of Ellahe on their claim of intentional interference, finding that they had not established that she had engaged in wrongful conduct with the purpose of preventing them from receiving the inheritance. The crucial issue was the standard of proof the jury had been instructed to apply. The trial judge had told jurors that the younger sisters needed to establish their claim through "clear and convincing evidence", a relatively demanding standard used in certain civil cases, including fraud claims.The sisters challenged that instruction on appeal, arguing that the court should instead have applied the lower standard of "preponderance of the evidence". Under this standard, a claim is established when the evidence makes it more likely than not that the alleged conduct occurred. The Appellate Court of Maryland agreed. In its October 28 opinion, written by Judge Kathryn Graeff, the court said the correct standard for intentional interference with an expected inheritance was preponderance of the evidence. It reasoned that the claim was closely related to other civil claims involving interference with economic interests, for which the lower standard applies.The court also referred to the legal framework adopted when Maryland first recognised intentional interference with an inheritance as a civil claim in 2020. That earlier decision had not specified the burden of proof. The appeals court said the standard should be consistent with the principles governing interference with economic expectations.It further explained that the incorrect instruction could have affected the jury's decision. Since jurors had been asked to apply a higher standard than the law required, the appeals court said it could not determine whether they might have reached a different conclusion under the correct test. It therefore reversed the judgment and sent the case back for further proceedings.The ruling does not establish that Ellahe committed fraud, manipulated her father or unlawfully took the money. Nor does it automatically award any portion of the trust to the younger sisters. Instead, it gives them another opportunity to pursue their inheritance-interference claim under the correct legal standard. The court did not need to decide other issues raised in the appeal, including disputes concerning expert handwriting evidence and testimony from the lawyer who drafted the trust.The case also highlights a legal distinction between challenging the validity of estate documents and claiming that someone deliberately interfered with an expected inheritance. While the younger sisters raised allegations of fraud and undue influence, the appellate decision focused on the standard of proof applicable to the interference claim. The next proceedings will determine whether the younger daughters can establish their allegations under the standard clarified by the appeals court.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient.
